content.text:
I now have the full pipeline. Here's the complete ordered account of what happens on `POST /api/owners`, driven by `owners.POST.yml` and its function classes. Every step runs under one shared transaction (`govern: [ transaction ]` on all steps).

## Gate (before any step)
- **Authorization** — `composition.authorize: "hasRole('OWNER_ADMIN')"`. Caller lacking `OWNER_ADMIN` is rejected (via `AuthorizationDeniedException`).

## Validations & side-effects, in pipeline order

1. **`ValidateOwnerFields`** — two layers:
   - **Bean validation** (`@Valid` on `OwnerFieldsDto`, runs first): `@NotNull` + `@Size` + `@Pattern` on `firstName` (letters, `^[\p{L}]+([ '-][\p{L}]+){0,2}$`, 1–30), `lastName` (similar, optional trailing `.`, 1–30), `@NotNull @Size(1..255)` `address`, `@NotNull @Size(1..80)` `city`, `@NotNull @Size(1..20)` `telephone`, `@Size(max 255)` `email`. Failures → `MethodArgumentNotValidException` (400).
   - **Blank/whitespace check** (catches values that slip past `@Size(min=1)`): requires non-blank `firstName`, `lastName`, `address` **checked in its normalized form**, `city`, `telephone`. Any missing → `MissingOwnerFieldsException` (400) listing each offending field.
   - *Side-effect:* publishes the validated body for later steps.

2. **`NormalizeOwnerTelephone`** — converts `telephone` to E.164 (strip non-digits; keep `+`/country code, else assume `+61` and drop one leading `0`). If result isn't a `+` followed by 8–15 digits → `InvalidTelephoneException` (400). *Side-effect:* writes canonical telephone back onto the body.

3. **`NormalizeOwnerEmail`** — `email` is optional: null/blank → set to `null`. If present, must match the email regex or → `InvalidEmailException` (400). *Side-effect:* stores it **lower-cased**.

4. **`NormalizeOwnerAddress`** — *Side-effect only:* rewrites `address` to canonical form (trim, collapse whitespace, upper-case, expand `ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`).

5. **`CheckOwnerTelephoneUnique`** — scans all owners; if any existing owner's telephone reduces to the same E.164 → `DuplicateTelephoneException` (409).

6. **`CheckOwnerHouseholdUnique`** — unless request sets `sharesHousehold=true`, rejects when an existing owner has the same **last name** (case-insensitive) **and normalized address** → `DuplicateHouseholdException` (409).

7. **`CheckOwnerCityCapacity`** — counts existing owners in the same city (case-insensitive, trimmed); if `>= 50` (`CAPACITY`) → `CityAtCapacityException` (409).

8. **`CheckOwnerDailyLimit`** — computes the effective business day (supplied `registrationDate` or today, rolled off weekends) and counts existing owners registered that day; if `>= 100` (`DAILY_LIMIT`) → `DailyOwnerLimitException` (429).

9. **`BuildOwner`** — *Side-effect:* maps DTO → `Owner` entity (via `OwnerMapper`) and sets `registrationDate` to the effective business day (weekend → next Monday).

10. **`CountNamesakes`** — *Side-effect:* sets `namesakeCount` = number of existing owners sharing the same first+last name (case-insensitive), excluding the new one.

11. **`AssignCustomerCode`** — *Side-effect:* sets `customerCode` = `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`, where `NNNN` is a per-city sequence = (owners already in that city) + 1.

12. **`AssignMembershipNumber`** — *Side-effect:* sets `membershipNumber` = `<customerCode>-M<YY>` (last two digits of registration year).

13. **`AssignHousehold`** — only when `sharesHousehold=true` **and** existing housemates (same last name + normalized address) exist: *Side-effect:* sets a stable `householdId` (SHA-256-derived) on the new owner **and back-fills + saves** each existing housemate that lacks it. Otherwise a no-op.

14. **`SaveOwner`** — *Side-effect:* persists the new owner via `ownerRepository.save`.

15. **`RespondWithOwnerCreated`** — *Side-effect:* maps to `OwnerDto` and responds **201 Created** with `Location: /api/owners/{id}`.

## Notes
- All fifteen steps share one transaction, so the whole thing commits once at the end (including the housemate back-fill saves in step 13); any escalation rolls it back.
- Order is deliberate: field validation → telephone/email/address normalization → uniqueness/capacity/rate checks (which compare against the *normalized* values) → entity build → derived-field assignment → persist → respond. Notably the address is normalized (step 4) before the household and customer-code logic reads it, and telephone is canonicalized (step 2) before the uniqueness check (step 5).

One caveat worth flagging: the uniqueness/capacity/daily-limit checks (steps 5–8) read via `ownerRepository.findAll()` and are not backed by a DB constraint, so under concurrent requests two owners could pass the same check before either saves — the single transaction doesn't serialize them against each other.

9. **`BuildOwner`** — *Side-effect:* maps DTO → `Owner` entity (via `OwnerMapper`) and sets `registrationDate` to the effective business day (weekend → next Monday).

10. **`CountNamesakes`** — *Side-effect:* sets `namesakeCount` = number of existing owners sharing the same first+last name (case-insensitive), excluding the new one.

11. **`AssignCustomerCode`** — *Side-effect:* sets `customerCode` = `<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>`, where `NNNN` is a per-city sequence = (owners already in that city) + 1.

12. **`AssignMembershipNumber`** — *Side-effect:* sets `membershipNumber` = `<customerCode>-M<YY>` (last two digits of registration year).

13. **`AssignHousehold`** — only when `sharesHousehold=true` **and** existing housemates (same last name + normalized address) exist: *Side-effect:* sets a stable `householdId` (SHA-256-derived) on the new owner **and back-fills + saves** each existing housemate that lacks it. Otherwise a no-op.

14. **`SaveOwner`** — *Side-effect:* persists the new owner via `ownerRepository.save`.

15. **`RespondWithOwnerCreated`** — *Side-effect:* maps to `OwnerDto` and responds **201 Created** with `Location: /api/owners/{id}`.

## Notes
- All fifteen steps share one transaction, so the whole thing commits once at the end (including the housemate back-fill saves in step 13); any escalation rolls it back.
- Order is deliberate: field validation → telephone/email/address normalization → uniqueness/capacity/rate checks (which compare against the *normalized* values) → entity build → derived-field assignment → persist → respond. Notably the address is normalized (step 4) before the household and customer-code logic reads it, and telephone is canonicalized (step 2) before the uniqueness check (step 5).

One caveat worth flagging: the uniqueness/capacity/daily-limit checks (steps 5–8) read via `ownerRepository.findAll()` and are not backed by a DB constraint, so under concurrent requests two owners could pass the same check before either saves — the single transaction doesn't serialize them against each other.
